mainTopic: Which foods can be used for the מצוה of מצה: the משנה's list of valid and invalid foods, and why טבל is excluded
overview: This amud opens by finishing an earlier point: מי פירות do not make dough into real חמץ. The גמרא then goes through the משנה's list of foods that can and cannot be used for מצה, asking about almost every case 'פשיטא, isn't it obvious?' דמאי works because anyone could make himself an עני through הפקר, and an עני may eat דמאי according to בית הלל. מעשר ראשון works even when the לוי took it from the stalks before תרומה גדולה, because of ריש לקיש's rule. אביי explains that grain on the stalks is not yet 'דגן', while grain in the pile is, so a לוי who took his share from the pile must still give תרומה גדולה. Redeemed מעשר שני and הקדש work even if the חומש was not paid. כהנים may use חלה and תרומה, because the repeated word 'מצות' includes them. Even rabbinic טבל, and מעשר שני or הקדש redeemed improperly (with an אסימון or with land), do not work. Finally, a ברייתא learns from 'לא תאכל עליו חמץ' that partly tithed טבל cannot be used for מצה. רב ששת explains that this follows רבי שמעון's rule אין איסור חל על איסור, and his source continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Fruit juice does not cause leavening
steps.stepSummary: This line closes the earlier discussion. מי פירות does not make dough become חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: And fruit juice does not cause leavening.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the topic it was just discussing. It states the rule that fruit juice does not make dough rise into real חמץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since fruit juice cannot cause true חימוץ, dough made with it is not full-fledged חמץ. This is the closing point of the previous discussion, before the גמרא moves on to new cases in the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Fruit juice; liquids that come from fruit
Cause dough to leaven and become חמץ

steps.whatToRemember: מי פירות do not make dough into real חמץ.

phrases.english: And fruit juice does not cause leavening.
phrases.notes: This line wraps up the discussion that came just before.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the discussion of liquids earlier
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Fruit juice cannot cause dough to become true חמץ.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: one can fulfill מצה with doubtfully tithed produce
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה. A person fulfills the מצוה of מצה with דמאי and with מעשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: A person fulfills his obligation with דמאי and with מעשר, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a new line from the משנה so it can discuss it. This step only sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה lists kinds of produce that may be used for מצה. These include דמאי, and מעשר ראשון whose תרומה was taken. The גמרא will now examine each case.

keyTerms.meaning: Fulfills his obligation
Produce bought from an עם הארץ that may not have been tithed; the חכמים require it to be tithed out of doubt
A tithe; here, מעשר ראשון, which is given to a לוי

phrases.english: One fulfills [the obligation] with doubtfully tithed produce and with tithe, etc.
phrases.notes: Here the גמרא is quoting our משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new case in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מצה made from דמאי or from properly treated מעשר fulfills the obligation.

steps.title: Challenge: doubtfully tithed produce is forbidden to him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how one can fulfill the מצוה with דמאי when he is not allowed to eat it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Doubtfully tithed produce is not fit for him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. דמאי that has not been tithed is forbidden to eat, so how can it count for מצה?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule is that מצה must be food the person is allowed to eat. The חכמים forbade eating untithed דמאי, so it seems this מצה should not count.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not fit for him; he may not eat it

steps.confusionAlert: דמאי is not definitely untithed (טבל ודאי). It is only a doubt, and the ban on eating it is דרבנן. This is why the next step can find a way around the problem.

phrases.english: Doubtfully tithed produce — it is not fit for him!
phrases.notes: The גמרא is raising a challenge here, not just stating a fact.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the משנה's ruling about דמאי
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that one fulfills מצה with דמאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: מצה must be permitted food, and untithed דמאי is forbidden to eat.

steps.title: Answer: he could make himself poor, so it counts as fit now
steps.stepSummary: A person could declare his property הפקר and become an עני, who may eat דמאי. So the דמאי is considered fit for him even now.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since, if he wanted, he could declare his property ownerless, become poor, and eat דמאי, it is fit for him now as well.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Because the person has an easy way to make the דמאי permitted to himself, it already counts as food that is fit for him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An עני is allowed to eat דמאי. Any person can become an עני by making all his property הפקר. Since that option is in his hands, the דמאי counts as fit for him now, even though he did not actually do it.

keyTerms.meaning: If he wants
Declares his property ownerless (הפקר)
A poor person
Now too

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a key idea: if something is permitted to a person through an option he could easily choose, it can count as fit for him even before he chooses it.

phrases.english: Since, if he wants, he can renounce ownership of his property
and become a poor person and eat doubtfully tithed produce,
phrases.notes: The poor are permitted to eat דמאי

phrases.english: now too it is fit for him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge about דמאי
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reframing what counts as fit: something that is potentially permitted through his own choice counts as fit
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Untithed דמאי is forbidden to him, so it cannot count for מצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since he can become an עני and eat דמאי, it counts as fit for him, and he fulfills the מצוה.

steps.title: Proof: one may feed the poor and soldiers doubtfully tithed produce
steps.stepSummary: A משנה teaches that one may feed דמאי to the poor and to אכסניא. This proves that the poor may eat דמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: As we learned in a משנה: One may feed the poor דמאי, and soldiers or lodgers דמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source for the claim in the answer that an עני may eat דמאי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer depended on one fact: an עני is permitted to eat דמאי. This משנה states that fact directly, so the answer stands on a solid source.

keyTerms.meaning: One may feed
Soldiers or travelers lodging in one's home

phrases.english: As we learned: One may feed the poor doubtfully tithed produce,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in מסכת דמאי.

phrases.english: and soldiers/lodgers doubtfully tithed produce.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the premise of the answer
steps.raayaObject: The claim that an עני may eat דמאי

steps.title: רב הונא: this משנה follows בית הלל
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא reports a ברייתא. בית שמאי forbid feeding דמאי to the poor and to אכסניא, and בית הלל permit it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב הונא said: It was taught: בית שמאי say one may not feed the poor or soldiers דמאי, and בית הלל say one may.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא adds background to the משנה just quoted. Its permission is actually the view of בית הלל, which is the view we follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that the poor may eat דמאי is part of a מחלוקת. Since halacha follows בית הלל, the proof stands, and the answer about דמאי and מצה holds.

keyTerms.meaning: The school of שמאי
The school of הלל, whose rulings are usually halacha

steps.whatToRemember: One can fulfill מצה with דמאי, because anyone could become an עני, and an עני may eat דמאי according to בית הלל.

phrases.english: And Rav Huna said: It was taught:
phrases.notes: The name of who said this is folded right into this line.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: אֵין מַאֲכִילִין אֶת הָעֲנִיִּים דְּמַאי
phrases.english: Beit Shammai say: One may not feed the poor doubtfully tithed produce
nor the soldiers/lodgers doubtfully tithed produce,
and Beit Hillel say: One may feed [them].
phrases.notes: Halacha follows בית הלל

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies whose opinion the proof-משנה follows
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Feeding דמאי to the poor and to אכסניא is a מחלוקת: בית שמאי forbid it, and בית הלל permit it.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה: מעשר ראשון whose תרומה was taken
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next case in the משנה: מעשר ראשון whose תרומת מעשר was removed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: First tithe whose תרומה was taken, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. This step sets up the question that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A לוי who receives מעשר ראשון must separate תרומת מעשר from it and give it to a כהן. The משנה says that once this is done, the מעשר ראשון may be used for מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: First tithe, given to a לוי
Its תרומה; here, תרומת מעשר, which the לוי gives to a כהן

phrases.english: First tithe whose teruma was taken, etc.
phrases.notes: Here the גמרא is quoting our משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next case in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מעשר ראשון whose תרומה was taken may be used for מצה.

steps.title: Challenge: isn't this obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the משנה is teaching. Once the תרומה is taken, the produce is plain חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is obvious! Since its תרומה was taken, it is non-sacred food!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why the משנה needed to say this case at all. The next step answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After תרומת מעשר is removed, מעשר ראשון has no remaining holiness and anyone may eat it. Of course it can be used for מצה, so the גמרא wants to know what new point the משנה is making.

keyTerms.meaning: It is obvious; why say it?
Non-sacred, ordinary food

phrases.aramaic: פְּשִׁיטָא! דְּכֵיוָן שֶׁנִּטְּלָה תְּרוּמָתוֹ חוּלִּין הָוֵי!
phrases.english: It is obvious! Since its teruma was taken, it is non-sacred!
phrases.notes: The answer comes next

steps.triggerLanguage: פְּשִׁיטָא! דְּכֵיוָן שֶׁנִּטְּלָה תְּרוּמָתוֹ חוּלִּין הָוֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why the משנה needed to state this case
steps.kashyaTarget: The need for the משנה's case of מעשר ראשון whose תרומה was taken
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Once the תרומה is removed the produce is plain חולין, so the ruling seems to teach nothing new.

steps.title: The case is when the Levite took his tithe early, from the stalks
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is needed for a case where the לוי took his מעשר ראשון while the grain was still on the stalks. He took off תרומת מעשר, but no תרומה גדולה was ever taken. This follows רבי אבהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, it is needed for a case where the לוי went first, while the grain was on the stalks. תרומת מעשר was taken from it, but תרומה גדולה was not taken from it. This follows רבי אבהו.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 8 by saying the משנה is talking about an unusual case. It is not the simple case where everything was done in the normal order.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally the כהן takes תרומה גדולה first, and only then does the לוי get מעשר ראשון. Here the לוי got his share early, so his portion never had תרומה גדולה removed. The new teaching is that this מעשר is still fully permitted, and so it can be used for מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: It is only needed for… (introduces a special case that explains why a teaching is necessary)
He went first, ahead of the normal order
Stalks or ears of grain that have not yet been threshed
The main תרומה, which the owner gives to the כהן
A tenth of the מעשר, which the לוי gives to the כהן

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that 'הקדימו' means the owner did something wrong. It means the לוי received his מעשר before the כהן received תרומה גדולה. That is the reverse of the usual order.

phrases.english: No, it is needed where he (the Levite) went first while it was on the stalks,
phrases.notes: The לוי took מעשר before the כהן took תרומה.

phrases.english: and the teruma of the tithe was taken from it,
but the great teruma was not taken from it,
and this is in accordance with Rabbi Abbahu.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 8's question about why the משנה needs to teach this case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: the משנה refers to a special case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think that מעשר which never had תרומה גדולה taken from it is forbidden, like טבל, and so cannot be used for מצה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Because of רבי אבהו's rule, such מעשר is exempt from תרומה גדולה. It counts as חולין and is fine for מצה.

steps.title: ריש לקיש's rule: tithe taken from the stalks is exempt from תרומה גדולה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו quotes רבי שמעון בן לקיש: מעשר ראשון taken early from the stalks is exempt from תרומה גדולה. The פסוק only obligates the לוי to give 'a tithe from the tithe', meaning תרומת מעשר, and nothing more.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said in the name of רבי שמעון בן לקיש: מעשר ראשון that the לוי took early, from the stalks, is exempt from תרומה גדולה. The פסוק says: 'And you shall separate from it a gift for ה׳, a tithe from the tithe.' ה׳ is saying: I told you to give a tithe from the tithe. I did not tell you to give תרומה גדולה plus a tithe from the tithe.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now quotes the actual teaching of רבי אבהו that it mentioned in Step 9. This is the source behind the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק that speaks to the לוי lists only one obligation: תרומת מעשר, 'a tithe from the tithe'. From this ריש לקיש learns that a לוי who took his share from the stalks owes nothing else. He does not have to make up the missing תרומה גדולה.

keyTerms.meaning: The first tithe, given to the לוי
Exempt
A tithe from the tithe, i.e. תרומת מעשר
As the פסוק says

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the rule that explains the whole case in the משנה. It also sets up רב פפא's question in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: As Rabbi Abbahu said that Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said:
First tithe that he took early, on the stalks,
is exempt from the great teruma,
as it is stated: 'And you shall set apart from it a gift for the Lord,
phrases.notes: במדבר יח:כו

phrases.english: a tithe from the tithe.'
'A tithe from the tithe' I told you (to give),

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא תְּרוּמָה גְּדוֹלָה וּתְרוּמַת מַעֲשֵׂר מִן הַמַּעֲשֵׂר.
phrases.english: and not the great teruma plus the teruma of the tithe from the tithe.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out the teaching of רבי אבהו that Step 9 relied on.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מעשר ראשון taken from the stalks before תרומה גדולה is exempt from תרומה גדולה. The source is the פסוק 'a tithe from the tithe'.

steps.title: רב פפא: then a tithe taken early from the pile should also be exempt
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges אביי: if the פסוק exempts the לוי, then even a לוי who took his share early from the pile (כרי) should be exempt from תרומה גדולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: If so, then even if the לוי went first when the grain was already in the pile, he should also be exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא pushes the rule further to test it. If the פסוק only requires 'a tithe from the tithe', why should it matter whether the grain was on stalks or already in a pile?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning from the פסוק says nothing about stalks. So it seems to exempt every early-taken מעשר, including grain that was already threshed and piled. That result seems wrong, so the rule needs a limit.

keyTerms.meaning: But if so… (introduces a challenge: following your logic leads to a strange result)
The pile of threshed, cleaned grain
Let it be exempt

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
But if that is so,
even if he took it early from the pile, let him also be exempt?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the rule in Step 10 reaches.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's reading of 'a tithe from the tithe'.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Taken at face value, the פסוק would exempt even מעשר taken from the pile, and that conclusion is unacceptable.

steps.title: אביי: another פסוק requires תרומה גדולה for the pile case
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that for the pile case, a different פסוק applies: 'From all your gifts you shall set apart all of ה׳'s תרומה.' This requires the לוי to give the missing תרומה גדולה.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: About your case, the פסוק says: 'From all your gifts you shall separate all of ה׳'s תרומה.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב פפא with a second פסוק. That פסוק requires תרומה גדולה when the לוי took his share from the pile.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'All of ה׳'s תרומה' tells the לוי he must also give the תרומה גדולה that is missing from his portion. So there are two פסוקים. One exempts the לוי and one obligates him, and each must apply to a different case.

keyTerms.meaning: About your case, the פסוק says…
Your gifts (what the לוי receives)
You shall separate (as תרומה)

phrases.english: He said to him: About your case the verse states:
'From all your gifts you shall set apart
phrases.notes: במדבר יח:כט

phrases.english: all of the Lord's teruma.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A second פסוק that covers the other case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'A tithe from the tithe' exempts every early-taken מעשר.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'All of ה׳'s תרומה' requires תרומה גדולה when the לוי took his share from the pile.

steps.title: Why does each verse go to its specific case?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: what made you apply the exemption to the stalks case and the obligation to the pile case, and not the other way around?
steps.simpleTranslation: And what did you see to make this distinction?
steps.whatsHappening: This is a short question that sets up the next step. It asks for the reason behind the way the two פסוקים were split between the two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two פסוקים pulling in opposite directions. The גמרא wants a logical reason why stalks get the exemption and the pile gets the obligation. Without one, the split could just as well be reversed.

keyTerms.meaning: And what did you see? (asks for the reason behind a distinction)

phrases.english: And what did you see (to distinguish this way)?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the split between the two פסוקים that was set up in Step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for applying the exemption to grain on the stalks and the obligation to grain in the pile.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's assignment of 'מעשר מן המעשר' to grain on the stalks and 'את כל תרומת ה׳' to grain in the pile
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Both פסוקים could apply to either case, so without a reason the split could just as well be reversed.

steps.title: Grain in the pile is finished 'grain', grain on the stalks is not
steps.stepSummary: Grain in the pile has already become 'דגן' (grain), so the כהן's right to תרומה has already taken hold. Grain on the stalks has not yet become דגן, so the לוי who takes it early is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one (in the pile) has become grain, and that one (on the stalks) has not become grain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for the split. It all depends on whether the produce has reached the stage the Torah calls 'דגן'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah gives תרומה to the כהן from 'דגנך', your grain. Once the grain is threshed and piled, it is called דגן, and the כהן's share is already attached to it. So the לוי must pay that share. On the stalks the grain is not yet דגן, so the כהן has no claim yet, and the לוי owes only תרומת מעשר.

keyTerms.meaning: It has become דגן (finished grain), and so it is now obligated in תרומה

steps.whatToRemember: A לוי who took his מעשר early, while the grain was on the stalks, is exempt from תרומה גדולה, because the grain was not yet 'דגן'. If he took it early from the pile, he must give תרומה גדולה. This is why the משנה's case of stalk-מעשר counts as fully permitted and can be used for מצה.

phrases.english: This (in the pile) has become grain,
and this (on the stalks) has not become grain.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A logical distinction based on how far the grain has been processed.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: There is no reason to prefer one way of splitting the two פסוקים.
steps.terutzMaskana: Once grain is piled it is דגן and is obligated in תרומה גדולה. On the stalks it is not yet דגן, so it is exempt.

steps.title: Isn't it obvious that redeemed second tithe and consecrated grain are fine?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that one can use redeemed מעשר שני and הקדש for מצה. It asks: isn't that obvious?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said one can use second tithe and consecrated grain that were redeemed. That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and asks why it even needed to be said. This sets up the next step, where the גמרא will find a case that is not obvious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once מעשר שני or הקדש is redeemed, it becomes regular חולין. Of course regular grain works for מצה. So why would the משנה bother teaching it?

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe, normally eaten in ירושלים, or redeemed for money
Property set aside for the בית המקדש
That were redeemed (bought back with money, so they lose their holiness)
It's obvious! (a challenge that the statement is not needed)

phrases.english: [The Mishnah said:] Second tithe and consecrated property that were redeemed, etc.
It's obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the תרומה גדולה discussion and returns to explaining the משנה's list of מצה rulings.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's need to state that redeemed מעשר שני and הקדש are valid for מצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Redeemed produce is plain חולין, so it obviously works. The statement seems pointless.

steps.title: The case is where the principal was paid but not the added fifth
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is talking about a case where only the main value was paid, without the extra fifth. It teaches that the missing fifth does not stop the redemption from working.
steps.simpleTranslation: What case are we dealing with here? Where he paid the principal but not the fifth. And it teaches us that the fifth does not hold back the redemption.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the משנה is teaching a special case: the person paid the basic value but still owes the extra חומש. Even so, the grain is already redeemed and can be used for מצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When an owner redeems his own מעשר שני or הקדש, he must add a fifth on top of the value. One might think that without the חומש the redemption is incomplete. The משנה teaches אין חומש מעכב: paying the קרן alone already makes the grain חולין. He still owes the fifth.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (introduces a specific scenario)
The principal, meaning the basic value
The extra fifth added when redeeming
Holds back or prevents (something from taking effect)
It teaches us (the new point)

steps.confusionAlert: אין חומש מעכב does NOT mean the חומש is optional. He still has to pay it. It only means that the redemption works even before he pays it.

phrases.english: With what are we dealing here?
Where he gave the principal
but did not give the fifth.
And it teaches us
that the fifth does not hold back [the redemption].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא by narrowing the משנה to a case that is not obvious.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Without the חומש, the redemption might be incomplete, so the grain would still be holy.
steps.terutzMaskana: אין חומש מעכב. Paying the קרן completes the redemption, so the grain may be used for מצה.

steps.title: Isn't it obvious that כהנים can use חלה and תרומה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that כהנים can use מצה of חלה and תרומה. It asks: isn't that obvious?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said the כהנים can use חלה and תרומה. That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next ruling of the משנה and asks why it was needed. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כהנים are allowed to eat חלה and תרומה. If they may eat it, why wouldn't it count as their מצה?

keyTerms.meaning: Priests
The portion of dough given to a כהן
The portion of produce given to a כהן

phrases.english: [The Mishnah said:] And the priests with challah and terumah, etc.
It's obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same pattern as step 15, applied to the next ruling in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that כהנים can use חלה and תרומה for מצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: כהנים may eat these foods, so they obviously work for the מצוה.

steps.title: The double word 'מצות' includes מצה not everyone may eat
steps.stepSummary: One might have thought that מצה must be food anyone may eat. The repeated word 'מצות' teaches that this is not required.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: we need מצה that is equal for every person. It teaches us: 'מצות', 'מצות' comes to include.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the possible mistake the משנה is preventing. Someone might think kosher מצה must be food that every Jew may eat.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חלה and תרומה are forbidden to a regular ישראל. So one might think they are not 'standard' מצה. The תורה repeats the word 'מצות', and the גמרא reads that repetition as a ריבוי (inclusion). It widens the rule to include מצה that only some people may eat.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said (introduces a mistaken assumption)
Equal for every person (food anyone may eat)
We require
Included or widened (a ריבוי from the פסוק)

phrases.english: What might you have said?
We require matzah that is equal for every person,
[so] it teaches us:
'Matzot', 'matzot': [the Torah] included.
phrases.notes: The word מצות appears more than once (דברים טז:ג, ח), which is read as including more cases.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא by showing what mistake the משנה prevents.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a mistaken assumption (מהו דתימא) and a פסוק that rejects it
steps.terutzHavaAmina: מצה must be food that every Jew may eat, so חלה and תרומה would not count.
steps.terutzMaskana: The repeated 'מצות' includes מצה that only some people may eat, so כהנים may use חלה and תרומה.

steps.title: Isn't it obvious that untithed produce doesn't work?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that one cannot use טבל for מצה. It asks: isn't that obvious?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: but not with untithed produce. That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next ruling and again asks why it needed to be said. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טבל is forbidden to eat. Food that is forbidden to eat obviously cannot be used for the מצוה of eating מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce from which the required gifts (תרומה, מעשר) have not yet been separated. It is forbidden to eat.

phrases.english: [The Mishnah said:] But not with untithed produce, etc.
It's obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same פשיטא pattern, now applied to the משנה's list of things that do NOT work.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that טבל is invalid for מצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: טבל is forbidden to eat, so it obviously cannot fulfill the מצוה.

steps.title: Even produce that is untithed only by rabbinic law doesn't work
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is needed for טבל that is only forbidden מדרבנן, like grain grown in a pot without a hole.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only for produce that is untithed by rabbinic law, such as grain he planted in a pot without a hole.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא says the משנה is teaching a less obvious case. It is talking about grain that is טבל only because of a rabbinic rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Grain grown in an עציץ שאינו נקוב is not attached to the ground, so מדאורייתא it needs no tithing. The רבנן still required tithing. One might think rabbinic טבל is good enough for a תורה מצוה. The משנה teaches that even this טבל cannot be used.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed only for [a specific case]
By rabbinic law (not from the תורה)
A plant pot with no hole, so it is not connected to the ground

phrases.english: No, it is necessary [only for this case]:
with produce that is untithed by rabbinic law,
where he planted it in an unperforated pot.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא by narrowing the משנה to rabbinic טבל.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the produce is permitted מדאורייתא, it might count for the תורה's מצוה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even טבל מדרבנן cannot be used for מצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a rabbinic prohibition on the food is enough to stop it from counting for a תורה-level מצוה of eating.

steps.title: Isn't it obvious that מעשר ראשון with its תרומה not taken doesn't work?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling about מעשר ראשון whose תרומה was not taken. It asks: isn't that obvious?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: and not with מעשר ראשון whose תרומה was not taken. That's obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the last ruling and asks why it was needed. The answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Produce with a gift still inside it is like טבל and is forbidden to eat. So of course it cannot be used for מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: First tithe, given to the לוי
Whose תרומה was not taken out of it

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא בְּמַעֲשֵׂר רִאשׁוֹן שֶׁלֹּא נִטְּלָה תְּרוּמָתוֹ.
phrases.english: [The Mishnah said:] And not with first tithe whose terumah was not taken.
It's obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Same פשיטא pattern, applied to the משנה's last ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's statement that מעשר ראשון whose תרומה was not taken is invalid
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Produce with an untaken gift is forbidden to eat, so it obviously cannot be used.

steps.title: The case is where the Levite took his tithe early from the pile
steps.stepSummary: The משנה is needed for the case where the לוי took his מעשר early from the pile, before the תרומה גדולה was taken. That produce is still forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is needed only where he took it early, from the pile.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers using the case discussed just before (steps 11-14): the לוי took his מעשר ראשון from the כרי before the כהן's תרומה גדולה was separated.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the produce is already called מעשר ראשון, so one might think nothing more is missing. But the earlier steps taught that once grain is in the pile it is דגן, and the כהן's right to תרומה גדולה has taken hold. So the תרומה גדולה is still inside this מעשר, and it cannot be used for מצה until it is taken.

keyTerms.meaning: He took it early (before the תרומה גדולה)
The pile of threshed grain

steps.whatToRemember: All four rulings follow one pattern: 'פשיטא!' is answered by a less obvious case. (1) The חומש does not hold back redemption. (2) The double 'מצות' includes כהן-only food. (3) Even rabbinic טבל is invalid. (4) מעשר taken early from the pile still needs its תרומה גדולה taken.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix this up with the stalks case. If the לוי took his tithe early from the stalks (שבלים), the תרומה גדולה is exempt, and this problem would not apply. Only the pile (כרי) case is meant here.

phrases.english: No, it is necessary [only for this case]:
where he took it early, in the pile.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the פשיטא by pointing to the הקדימו בכרי case from steps 11-14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the produce already has the status of מעשר ראשון, it might be considered fully fixed and permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: מעשר ראשון taken early from the pile still contains the תרומה גדולה, so it cannot be used for מצה until that is separated.
steps.whyThisMatters: It ties the משנה back to the earlier rule: in the pile, the grain is already דגן, so the כהן's share has taken hold.

steps.title: The משנה follows אביי's answer to רב פפא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the משנה had to teach the case of the early-taken מעשר ראשון. Without it, one might follow רב פפא's suggestion. The משנה teaches the distinction אביי gave in reply.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have thought the rule follows what רב פפא suggested to אביי. So the משנה teaches us the rule according to אביי's answer to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes the answer from the last step. It explains what mistake the משנה is protecting us from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: As taught earlier on this amud (steps 10-14), a לוי who takes his מעשר while the grain is still on the stalks is exempt from תרומה גדולה. רב פפא asked אביי: why not also exempt him when he takes it from the pile? אביי answered that grain in a pile is already 'דגן' and owes תרומה, so it is different. Our משנה confirms אביי: produce taken from the pile is still forbidden, so it cannot be used for מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Lest you say / you might have thought (introduces a mistaken assumption)
It teaches us (introduces the correct rule)
He answered him (gave a distinction in reply)

phrases.english: Lest you say
as Rav Pappa said to Abaye,
phrases.notes: רב פפא suggested that even grain taken from the pile should be exempt from תרומה גדולה.

phrases.english: it teaches us
as he answered him.
phrases.notes: אביי answered by splitting the two cases: on the stalks the grain is exempt, but in the pile it is obligated.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא כְּדַאֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the תירוץ of step 22 by naming the mistaken idea the משנה rules out.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the mistaken assumption (רב פפא's idea) that makes the משנה necessary
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Like רב פפא, one might think that מעשר taken from the pile is also exempt from תרומה גדולה.
steps.terutzMaskana: Like אביי, grain in a pile already owes תרומה. So that produce stays forbidden and cannot be used for מצה.

steps.title: Isn't it obvious that unredeemed second tithe and consecrated grain don't work?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next ruling of the משנה: מעשר שני and הקדש that were not redeemed cannot be used for מצה. It asks why this needs to be said.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And not with מעשר שני or הקדש that were not redeemed, etc.' But that is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next case in the משנה and asks the same question again: why state something obvious?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unredeemed מעשר שני may not be eaten outside ירושלים, and unredeemed הקדש is holy and may not be eaten at all. Food you may not eat obviously cannot be used for the מצוה of eating מצה. So the משנה seems to teach nothing new.

keyTerms.meaning: Second tithe; eaten in ירושלים, or redeemed with money
Property consecrated to the Temple
They were redeemed (their holiness was moved onto money)
It is obvious! (a challenge that a teaching is unnecessary)

phrases.english: And not with second tithe
or consecrated property that was not redeemed, etc.
phrases.notes: Here the גמרא is quoting our משנה.

phrases.english: Isn't that obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Repeats the same 'isn't it obvious' pattern (as in steps 19 and 21) for the next case in the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that unredeemed מעשר שני and הקדש cannot be used for מצה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Food that is forbidden to eat clearly cannot fulfill a מצוה of eating, so the ruling seems unnecessary.

steps.title: Not redeemed properly: second tithe redeemed with an unminted coin
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה means items that were redeemed, but not in the correct way. The first example is מעשר שני redeemed with an אסימון (a metal blank with no stamped image). This does not work, because the פסוק requires money with a צורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Really, the case is where they were redeemed. What does 'not redeemed' mean? Not redeemed according to halacha. For example, מעשר שני redeemed with an unminted coin. The Torah says 'וצרת הכסף', which means something that has a form (צורה).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by reading the משנה's words in a new way. 'Not redeemed' means 'not redeemed properly'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think any attempt at redemption takes away the holiness. The גמרא reads 'וצרת' as connected to 'צורה', so the redemption money must be a minted coin with an image. An אסימון has no image, so the redemption fails. The produce is still מעשר שני and cannot be used for מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually / really (starts a new reading of the text)
According to their halacha / in the proper way
An unminted metal blank with no image
'And you shall bind up the money' (דברים 14:25)
A form / stamped image on a coin

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'שלא נפדו' as 'never redeemed at all'. The גמרא says the owner did try to redeem the items. The attempt simply failed halachically.

phrases.english: Actually, where they were redeemed,
and what does 'not redeemed' mean?
that they were not redeemed properly:

phrases.aramaic: מַעֲשֵׂר שֵׁנִי שֶׁפְּדָאוֹ עַל גַּב אֲסִימוֹן,
phrases.english: second tithe that he redeemed with an unminted coin,
for the Merciful One said: 'and bind up the money'
phrases.notes: The word וצרת is read as connected to צורה (form).

phrases.english: something that has a form.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 24 by giving the משנה's words a narrower meaning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the משנה's wording ('not redeemed' means 'not properly redeemed')
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think any act of redemption removes the holiness of מעשר שני, even with an unminted coin.
steps.terutzMaskana: Redemption with an אסימון fails because the coin must have a צורה. The produce stays מעשר שני and cannot be used for מצה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets a basic rule of פדיון מעשר שני: only minted coins with a stamped image can be used.

steps.title: Not redeemed properly: consecrated property redeemed with land
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives the הקדש example of an improper redemption. Someone redeemed it with land instead of money. This fails, because the פסוק says 'ונתן הכסף וקם לו', so redemption must be done with money.
steps.simpleTranslation: And הקדש that he redeemed with land does not count. The Torah says: 'And he will give the money and it shall be established for him.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the same answer and explains the second item in the משנה, הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the redemption is done with 'כסף', which means money or movable value, not land. So if someone tries to move הקדש's holiness onto a field, nothing happens. The grain stays holy and cannot be used for מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: He redeemed it (moved its holiness onto something else)
Land / real estate
'And he will give the money and it shall be established for him'

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's 'not redeemed' cases are about failed redemptions. מעשר שני needs a coin with a צורה, not an אסימון. הקדש needs money, not land. In both cases the holiness stays, so the grain cannot be used for מצה.

phrases.english: and consecrated property that he redeemed with land,
for the Merciful One said:
'and he will give the money and it shall be established for him.'
phrases.notes: Redemption of הקדש must be done with money, not land.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the תירוץ of step 25 by applying the same 'improper redemption' idea to הקדש.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the משנה's wording, applied to the second item
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think redeeming הקדש with land removes its holiness.
steps.terutzMaskana: Redemption with land fails because the פסוק requires כסף. The grain stays holy and cannot be used for מצה.

steps.title: A ברייתא about using untithed produce for מצה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא that asks whether a person can fulfill the מצוה of מצה with טבל that was not fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: I might have thought that a person fulfills his obligation of מצה with טבל that was not fixed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new ברייתא on the same topic as the משנה, which is what food can be used for מצה. This line sets things up, and the גמרא will immediately question its wording.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טבל is produce from which the required gifts have not yet been separated. The ברייתא opens with 'יכול', meaning 'you might have thought', which signals that it will soon reject this idea and bring a source.

keyTerms.meaning: I might have thought; this introduces an idea that will be rejected
His obligation, here the מצוה of eating מצה
Produce that has not yet been tithed and is forbidden to eat
Fixed, meaning the gifts were separated so the produce may be eaten

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
I might think a person fulfills his obligation
with untithed produce that was not fixed.
phrases.notes: The ברייתא's sentence continues with 'מנין' in step 29.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: יָכוֹל יוֹצֵא אָדָם יְדֵי חוֹבָתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the משנה's list (מעשר שני, הקדש) to a ברייתא about טבל and מצה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ברייתא raises the idea that one could fulfill the מצוה of מצה with unfixed טבל, an idea it will reject.

steps.title: All טבל is unfixed, so why say it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's wording: 'טבל that was not fixed' seems to repeat itself, since all טבל is unfixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But all טבל is also not fixed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the wording of the ברייתא. Saying 'טבל that was not fixed' looks extra, because that is simply what טבל means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once produce is fixed, it is no longer טבל. So the words 'that was not fixed' must be teaching something more specific. The challenge forces a new reading of which case the ברייתא means.

keyTerms.meaning: Also
Behold, but surely

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל טֶבֶל נָמֵי הָא לֹא נִתְקַן!
phrases.english: But all untithed produce is also not fixed!

steps.triggerLanguage: כׇּל טֶבֶל נָמֵי הָא לֹא נִתְקַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wording of the ברייתא quoted in step 27.
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'בטבל שלא נתקן' in the ברייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The phrase is redundant, because by definition all טבל is unfixed.

steps.title: It means produce that was only partly tithed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads the ברייתא as speaking about produce that had some gifts taken but not all of them, even if only מעשר עני is missing, and asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, it means טבל that was not completely fixed: תרומה גדולה was taken but not תרומת מעשר; or מעשר ראשון was taken but not מעשר שני; or even only מעשר עני is missing. From where do we know it cannot be used?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the wording problem. The ברייתא means produce that was partly fixed but not fully fixed, and the ברייתא then asks for a source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even if only one gift is missing, the produce is still טבל and still forbidden. This holds even when only מעשר עני is missing, which has no holiness and is just a gift to the poor. 'מנין' asks for the פסוק that excludes this produce from use as מצה.

keyTerms.meaning: Completely, fully
The first gift to the כהן, separated from the whole crop
The tenth of the לוי's מעשר, given to a כהן
The tithe for the poor, given in certain years instead of מעשר שני
From where do we know?

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think that partly tithed produce is 'mostly permitted'. As long as even one required gift, even מעשר עני, has not been separated, it is fully טבל.

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: בְּטֶבֶל שֶׁלֹּא נִתְקַן כׇּל צוֹרְכּוֹ.
phrases.english: Rather: with untithed produce that was not completely fixed.
from which the great תרומה was taken
but the תרומה of the tithe was not taken from it,
or the first tithe but not the second tithe,
and even the poor man's tithe; from where do we know this?
phrases.notes: 'Even מעשר עני' means even if only that tithe is missing.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא: בְּטֶבֶל שֶׁלֹּא נִתְקַן כׇּל צוֹרְכּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the wording challenge of step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the case (אוקימתא) of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Not fixed' seemed to describe ordinary טבל, which made it redundant.
steps.terutzMaskana: It refers to partly fixed טבל, which is still forbidden even if only מעשר עני is missing.

steps.title: The פסוק: only food whose problem is חמץ
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves from 'לא תאכל עליו חמץ' that מצה must be food whose only possible איסור is חמץ, which excludes טבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'Do not eat חמץ with it'. This means food whose איסור comes from 'do not eat חמץ'. That excludes this food, whose איסור does not come from חמץ but from 'do not eat טבל'.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives its source from the פסוק. You fulfill מצה only with food that would be forbidden only because of חמץ, not food that is already forbidden as טבל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק links מצה with חמץ, so the food used for מצה must be food that becomes forbidden through חמץ. טבל is already forbidden for a different reason, so it is excluded.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches
Do not eat חמץ with it (דברים ט״ז:ג)
This excludes
Its prohibition

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basic rule for what qualifies as מצה: it must be dough that could become חמץ and is not already forbidden for another reason.

phrases.english: The verse states: 'Do not eat leavened bread with it'

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁאִיסּוּרוֹ מִשּׁוּם ״בַּל תֹּאכַל עָלָיו חָמֵץ״,
phrases.english: food whose prohibition is due to 'do not eat leavened bread with it',

phrases.aramaic: יָצָא זֶה שֶׁאֵין אִיסּוּרוֹ מִשּׁוּם ״בַּל תֹּאכַל חָמֵץ״,
phrases.english: this excludes food whose prohibition is not due to 'do not eat leavened bread',
but due to 'do not eat untithed produce'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the ברייתא's 'מנין' question from step 29.
steps.raayaObject: That partly tithed טבל cannot be used for מצה

steps.title: Where did the חמץ prohibition go?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the ברייתא says טבל is forbidden only as טבל. If it leavens, it should also be forbidden as חמץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the איסור of חמץ, where did it go?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא's reasoning. Why does the ברייתא treat טבל as not forbidden because of חמץ? טבל dough that rises should be חמץ too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא assumed that טבל's only איסור is טבל. The גמרא points out that the חמץ prohibition should also apply on top of it. If it does, טבל would fit 'forbidden because of חמץ' and should qualify.

keyTerms.meaning: Prohibition (Aramaic)
Where did it go?

phrases.english: And the prohibition of leavened bread, where did it go?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reasoning of the derivation in step 30.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's claim that טבל is forbidden only because of טבל and not because of חמץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The חמץ prohibition should apply to טבל as well, so טבל would also be 'forbidden because of חמץ'.

steps.title: רב ששת: the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת answers that the ברייתא follows רבי שמעון, who holds אין איסור חל על איסור, so חמץ does not take effect on טבל. The גמרא then begins to quote רבי שמעון's source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Whose view is this? It is רבי שמעון, who said one איסור does not take effect on another איסור. As it was taught, רבי שמעון says:
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the question by tying the ברייתא to רבי שמעון's rule. The last line, 'דתניא', sets up the ברייתא that shows רבי שמעון's view, which continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: טבל is already forbidden, so according to רבי שמעון the later חמץ prohibition cannot take effect on it. Its only איסור therefore stays טבל, and the פסוק excludes it. This means the ברייתא's reasoning works only according to רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: Whose view is this?
A second prohibition does not take effect on something already prohibited

steps.whatToRemember: טבל cannot be used for מצה because its only איסור is טבל. According to רבי שמעון (אין איסור חל על איסור), חמץ never takes effect on it, so it is not 'forbidden because of חמץ'.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule אין איסור חל על איסור comes up all over ש״ס. Here it decides whether טבל can count as possible חמץ, and so whether it can be used as מצה.

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
Whose view is this? It is Rabbi Shimon,

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר: אֵין אִיסּוּר חָל עַל אִיסּוּר.
phrases.english: who said: a prohibition does not take effect on a prohibition.
As it was taught: Rabbi Shimon says:
phrases.notes: This just sets things up; the ברייתא itself continues on the next amud.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 31 by naming the תנא behind the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attributing the ברייתא to a specific תנא (רבי שמעון)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חמץ prohibition should also apply to טבל, which would undercut the ברייתא.
steps.terutzMaskana: According to רבי שמעון, אין איסור חל על איסור, so חמץ does not take effect on טבל and its only איסור remains טבל.
